`replace()` replaces every match only if the regex has the `g` flag, and one letter at the end of a pattern is easy to miss. `replaceAll()` says it in the name.

The rule also reports a regex passed to `replaceAll()` when it matches only one fixed string, because a plain string does the same and needs no escaping.

`--fix` renames the method, and turns the regex into a string where the regex matches one fixed string.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```js
const slug = title.replace(/\s+/g, "-");
const path = name.replaceAll(/\./g, "/");
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const slug = title.replaceAll(/\s+/g, "-");
const path = name.replaceAll(".", "/");

const first = title.replace(/\s+/, "-");
```
